ABSTRACT. We prove that, whenever 𝛼, 𝛽 > 0 and 𝛼/𝛽 is irrational, every sufficiently large integer is a sum
of distinct indexed terms of the two sequences ( ⌊2𝑛𝛼⌋) 𝑛≥0 and ( ⌊2𝑛 𝛽⌋) 𝑛≥0. This answers the doubling
case of Erdős Problem 354 affirmatively. The proof associates a symbolic tower system to each sequence
and turns infinitely many missing sums into a nonproduct invariant coupling. Binary carries give two
complementary estimates: many marked transitions force decay of correlations, whereas a single common
marked transition controls one-step displacement by displacement at a prescribed large time. The latter
estimate forces a forward relation between the positions of binary ones in the two parameters. Applying
that relation in both directions bounds all zero runs, contradicting the correlation estimate. A complete
Lean 4 formalization of the exact conjecture accompanies the paper; its final theorem has no admitted
proof and uses only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
1. INTRODUCTION
A sequence of nonnegative integers is called complete if its finite subsequence sums contain every
sufficiently large integer. The number of summands is unrestricted, but each index may be used at most
once. The question considered here appears in the study of complete sequences initiated by Graham [ 4]
and is recorded by Erdős and Graham [ 2, p. 58]. It is Problem 354 in Bloom’s catalogue [ 1]. Earlier
investigations include Hegyvári [ 5]; his later discussion [ 6] also describes the connection with binary
bracket sequences.
